RESULT: The change in log-odds of remission for each 1-year increase in patient age is -0.0795 (95% CI -0.131 to -0.028), i.e., each additional year of age is associated with a decrease of about 0.08 in the log-odds of remission (OR ≈ 0.924, p = 0.0025), holding BMI and gender fixed in a logistic regression on n = 80 complete cases.

FULL COEFFICIENT TABLE (logit(remission) ~ Age + BMI + C(Gender), Female reference; statsmodels Logit, n=80, converged=True in 5 iterations, pseudo R² = 0.124, LLR p = 0.0033):
- Age: coef -0.0795, SE 0.0263, z -3.02, p 0.0025, 95% CI [-0.1311, -0.0280]; OR 0.924 (95% CI 0.877-0.972)
- BMI: coef 0.1621, SE 0.1088, z 1.49, p 0.1363, 95% CI [-0.0512, 0.3754]; OR 1.176
- Gender [Male vs Female]: coef -0.6132, SE 0.5471, z -1.12, p 0.2624, 95% CI [-1.6855, 0.4591]; OR 0.542
- Intercept: 1.5313, SE 2.7755, p 0.5811

Key numbers: Age log-odds coefficient per year = -0.0795; SE = 0.0263; 95% CI = [-0.131, -0.028]; p = 0.0025; OR = 0.924.

Sensitivity note (alternative remission = PR+SD, disease control): Age coefficient = -0.0605 (SE 0.0283, p 0.033, OR 0.941) — direction and significance are robust, magnitude modestly smaller than under the PR-only definition.
